The pure class interface. 
public abstract class Aggregate<A>
  implements Formattable
The abstract superclass of all aggregate classes. It provides methods with default implementations for traversing the contents of an aggregate.

Version: $Id: Aggregate.pizza,v 1.3 1997/11/09 23:02:58 wg Exp $

reduce

public <B> B reduce(B z,
                    (B, A) -> B f);
Reduce elements of aggregate. 
 
  AGG{x1, x2, ..., xn}.reduce(z, f) = f(...f(f(z,x1), x2)..., xn)
Reduction order is determined by enumeration order.

fold

public A fold((A, A) -> A f)
  throws NoSuchElementException;
Fold elements of aggregate. 
 
  AGG{x1, x2, ..., xn}.fold(f) = f(...f(x1, x2)..., xn)
  AGG{x1}.fold(f) = x1
Folding order is determined by enumeration order. @throws NoSuchElementException if aggregate is empty

compare

public int compare((A, A) -> int ecompare,
                   Aggregate<A> other);
Lexicographical ordering of aggregates according to there enumerated elements. Produces a total order, provided the element ordering is total. Note, however, that this total ordering does not necessarily coincides with equality. This is only the case if 
 x === y ==> x.enumerate() === y.enumerate()

See also:

compact

public void compact();
Compact this aggregate. This method has no semantic effect, but for some aggregate implementations it frees auxiliary memory allocated for the internal representation.
